title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: AUGIE'S ROOTS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Augie Lindqvist, a water meter reader from Evansville, Indiana.
Augie knows every dog on every street in town.
But past his own dad, he knew nothing about his family.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE QUESTION
segments.quote: To be ignorant of what occurred before you were born is to remain always a child.
segments.author: Cicero
lines: At Sunday dinner, his granddaughter Mia asked where the Lindqvists came from.
Augie said, Evansville. Pass the gravy.
Mia read him a line from Cicero, the Roman speaker:
To be ignorant of what occurred before you were born is to remain always a child.
Augie was sixty-three. Not a child. So he started digging.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LIBRARY
segments.quote: Knowledge is of two kinds. We know a subject ourselves, or we know where we can find information upon it.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: At the library, he wandered like a lost tourist.
Over the family history desk hung a sign from Samuel Johnson, the English writer:
Knowledge is of two kinds. We know a subject ourselves, or we know where we can find information upon it.
So he asked. Mrs. Odom, the librarian, sat him at a microfilm machine.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE SEA CAPTAIN
segments.author: John Adams
lines: Family legend said Great-Grandpa Gus was a Swedish sea captain.
The records said Gus Lindqvist, barber, nineteen ten. Not even a rowboat.
Augie argued with the machine. Mrs. Odom quoted John Adams:
Facts are stubborn things.
So he went looking for the barber he had.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BASEMENT
segments.quote: No man who has once heartily and wholly laughed can be altogether irreclaimably bad.
segments.author: Thomas Carlyle
lines: An old newspaper told the rest.
Gus made moonshine in his basement, until his wife Hilda poured it in the Ohio River. In her Sunday hat.
Augie laughed until he cried. Mia read him a line from Thomas Carlyle, the Scottish writer:
No man who has once heartily and wholly laughed can be altogether irreclaimably bad.
Gus was no captain. He was a barber with a twinkle.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: LANE TWELVE
segments.quote: Every man takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world.
segments.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
lines: Then Mia's DNA kit came back. Third cousin: Stan Kowalczyk.
His bowling rival for twenty years.
His wife June read the magnet on their fridge, from Arthur Schopenhauer, the German thinker:
Every man takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world.
On bowling night, Augie walked over and said, Hello, cousin. Stan dropped his ball. On his foot.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BOOK
segments.quote: People will not look forward to posterity, who never look backward to their ancestors.
segments.author: Edmund Burke
lines: Augie typed it all up. Forty pages, one typo per page.
On page one, he wrote a line from Edmund Burke, the Irish statesman:
People will not look forward to posterity, who never look backward to their ancestors.
In June, forty-one cousins had a picnic by the river. Stan brought potato salad.
And Augie left blank pages at the back, for Mia's kids someday.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Ask. Know where to look. Face the facts. Laugh. Look past your lane. Write it down.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Ask where you come from. Know where to look. Face the facts. Laugh. Look past your lane. Write it down.
I looked up my own family once. We've told the same three jokes since eighteen ninety.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
